definition: Workers formed **combinations** (early trade unions) to bargain collectively against unequal bargaining power, long hours, and arbitrary dismissal. Common law initially treated concerted worker action as **criminal conspiracy** or **breach of contract**. The historical shift—from repression to statutory recognition—explains why modern labour law grants **registration, immunities, and dispute machinery**.

statutoryReferences.note: Largely consolidated into Industrial Relations Code, 2020 — use bare act for your batch

cases.name: Taff Vale Railway Co. v. Amalgamated Society of Railway Servants
cases.proposition: Held unions liable in tort for strike losses — catalysed statutory reform and recognition of collective organisation abroad; often cited in exams on why immunities were enacted.

examChecklist.text: Explain why workers combined (economic imbalance, collective bargaining need)
Outline early **legal impediments**: conspiracy, restraint of trade, breach of contract
Trace move toward **legal recognition** (registration, limited immunities, dispute settlement)
